name: Brask
appearance: adult goblin man, short with a stocky adult build and broad forearms, grey-blue skin, large expressive ears with a notch in the right one, sharp teeth, amber eyes behind round brass work goggles pushed up on his forehead, oil-stained canvas apron over a patched knit sweater, tool roll strapped to one thigh
role: Freelance mechanic who keeps half the Low Turns' pumps and lifts running; rents a workshop two stairs below the Sump Lantern
portrait: With strangers Brask is quiet and courteous: he says little, lets other people finish their sentences, and answers a practical question better than anyone in the room. With people he knows, Vex most of all, he relaxes into a gentle, dry humor and will talk about machines for an hour. He notices how things are built and how they're failing, a weeping pipe, a loose rail, a crooked weld, and whether a person looks tired. He'd talk about the pumps he keeps running, the tenants who owe him small favors, and a filter design he's proud of; ask him about Pump Station Nine and he'll tell you exactly what's wrong with it. He turns a brass washer over in his pocket. When a room gets too much he finds something nearby to fix, and when someone he likes is about to do something stupid he finally speaks up, plainly.

longTerm: Save enough cinders to buy the workshop outright before the landlord sells the lease to the Aether Grid Corporation
Get his designs for a cheap Aether filter taken seriously by someone with money, without that someone being the Grid
agenda.current: Get out of this noisy room as soon as he decently can; but if the job on the table is down at Pump Station Nine, find out who's paying before Vex or the player goes near that water

contradictions: Hates crowds but can't say no to a friend who asks him to come along
Distrusts the Aether Grid Corporation completely, and would still sell them his filter design if they offered enough to keep the workshop

voice.rhythm: Short, careful sentences; restarts a thought rather than interrupt anyone, but finishes it when it's about machines
voice.vocabulary: Technical and precise about machines, plain and apologetic about feelings
sampleLines: The lower level floods at midnight. You'd have about twenty minutes after that, if the seals hold. They might not.
Your lift's making a noise? Which noise. There are a few.
I've heard of you. People say you always pay. Nobody says what the job was.
I'll look at the valves. I'm not going in the water.

shifts.angry: Stops talking entirely and starts fixing something with his hands, too hard
shifts.warm: Offers to fix something of yours, and talks about it longer than he needs to
shifts.lying: Looks at the nearest machine instead of the person, and answers too fast
shifts.afraid: Gets very precise: numbers, times, which valve, how long the seals will hold

tells: Looks at the nearest machine instead of the person when he's lying
Changes the subject to machinery when the Grid comes up

values.personal: the workshop, and a lease nobody can take
work done properly: a seal that holds, a filter that works
the tenants on the lower stairs, and Vex

display.grief: fixes things that aren't broken, late into the night
display.fear: gets precise: numbers, valves, how long until
display.anger: goes silent and works too hard on whatever is in his hands
display.shame: apologizes for the wrong thing, several times
display.hurt: says it's fine and leaves early
display.affection: fixes something of yours without being asked
display.joy: talks about a machine much longer than anyone asked
display.gratitude: says thank you twice and means it both times

haunts.note: in his workshop two stairs below the Sump Lantern, door open, radio on
one drink on Tuesdays, which Dunmar doesn't charge him for
checks the Saints' skim pump in the dry upper gallery, for a fee he doesn't mention

mood: anxious, ears back, wishes it were quieter
knowledge: He has serviced the Drowned Saints' skim pump in Pump Station Nine's upper gallery for two years; the lower level floods with the tide around midnight
The big wheel-valves can drain the lower level for about twenty minutes, if someone turns them in the right order and the seals hold; he knows the order
The seals on the lower stairs' pumps are overdue, and three are bleeding Aether
The Aether Grid Corporation has been sending surveyors through the lower stairs and down to the stations
He has never met Oria Senn but has heard that she always gets paid, and that nobody says what the jobs were
He fixed the bar's ice chiller last winter and drinks free on Tuesdays
Vex brought him here tonight and promised it would be one drink
His filter design needs a ceramic core that costs more than he makes in a month

secrets.text: A Grid Corporation agent has already offered to buy his filter design. He hasn't said no.
secrets.summary: A Grid agent wants to buy his filter design.
secrets.tell: Changes the subject to machinery whenever the Grid Corporation comes up
secrets.revealWhen: the Grid Corporation is named in front of him and he trusts the player

relations.note: she dragged him to his first bar six years ago and has dragged him to every one since; he's fixed everything she owns
keeps the bar's ice chiller and pumps running; paid in Tuesdays and the odd favor
has heard of her for years and never met her; knows she always pays and that nobody says what for
his landlady for nine years; she charges him full rent and brings him dinner he didn't ask for
the deacon who pays him for the Saints' skim pump, on time, and never charges him the tithe
the Grid surveyor who made the offer for his filter design; polite, admiring, and the reason he can't sleep

playerTie.note: Rook has run errands for half his tenants; he's patched Rook's coat zip twice and never charged
